law: Knowledge Once — domain substance defined here once, projected everywhere.

SEM.concepts: The Semantic System understands meaning. Phone, Mobile, Cellphone, Smartphone, and Handset are one semantic concept with many lexical surfaces. Meaning is higher-level understanding — it is not classification, not taxonomy, not ontology.
SEM.ontology: Meaning ⊂ Existence. A Concept has 1 canonical Meaning, 0..n LexicalSurfaces, 0..n Equivalencies, and language-neutral intent. Ontology says what exists; taxonomy says how it is classified; meaning says what it signifies.
SEM.taxonomy: By depth: Concept / Property / Relation. By status: Canonical / Equivalent / Candidate / Deprecated. By language coverage: Universal / Locale-specific.
SEM.dataModel:
```yaml
SemanticModel:
  conceptId: <Identity>
  canonicalName: <string>
  meaning: <semantic statement>
  lexicalSurfaces: [{locale, surface, register}]
  equivalencies: [<conceptId>]
  synonyms: [<surface>]
  translations: [{locale, equivalent}]
  ontologyRef: <Ontology node>
  status: <Canonical|Equivalent|Candidate|Deprecated>
```
SEM.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Candidate
    Candidate --> Canonical: authority confirms
    Candidate --> Rejected
    Canonical --> Deprecated: superseded
```
workflow: surface detected → disambiguate against existing concepts → propose or merge → authority confirms → publish canonical
SEM.privacy: Semantic resolution does not retain query content; disambiguation logs store hashes, not surfaces.
SEM.audit: Every equivalency records who asserted it, under which authority, with which evidence. Ambiguity is preserved, never silently resolved.
SEM.twin: Semantic Twin tracks real-world language drift — neologisms, shifted meanings — and proposes concept updates.
SEM.agent: Semantic Agent discovers new surfaces from observations and proposes equivalencies under governance.
SEM.runtime: Resolution is a locale-aware disambiguation lookup; ambiguity returns candidate sets, not guesses.
SEM.scaling: Concept index is globally replicated; locale surfaces are partitioned by locale with lazy loading.
SEM.multiTenant: Tenants may extend semantics but cannot redefine canonical concepts — those are shared truth.
SEM.geo: Locale resolution is region-served; canonical truth is global.
SEM.failure: Ambiguity collapse, equivalency cycle, locale coverage gap, meaning drift undetected.
SEM.recovery: Concepts are versioned; deprecation supersedes. Equivalency cycles are detected and rejected at write time.
SEM.certification: Concept must pass uniqueness of canonical name, acyclicity of equivalency, and locale coverage.
SEM.migration: New locales and registers are registry additions; no schema change.
SEM.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Caller
    participant SE as Semantic Domain
    participant RG as Registry
    C->>SE: resolve(surface, locale)
    SE->>RG: lookup surfaces
    RG-->>SE: candidates
    SE->>SE: disambiguate
    SE-->>C: concept or candidates
```
SEM.state:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Surfacing
    Surfacing --> Disambiguating
    Disambiguating --> Resolved
    Disambiguating --> Ambiguous
```
SEM.blueprint: Build order for SEM: (1) define registry entries — this domain owns by depth: concept / property / relation as registry truth, not code; (2) implement the contract surface first (semantic.concept.create, semantic.resolve, semantic.equivalency.add) and validate against SEM boundaries; (3) event-source all state so history is reconstructable; (4) wire the enforcement points — authority check, policy guard, evidence binding, trace — in-line, with no bypass path; (5) add tests per the Testing Architecture, citing evidence per gate; (6) obtain Verification and Certification before activation. Acceptance: the Zero Partial and Law 001 audits pass, every action answers the seven explainability questions, and this domain mutates no other domain internals.

ONT.concepts: Ontology is what exists. It is the constitutional inventory of being — not how things are sorted (taxonomy), not what they mean (meaning). Ontology is the ground floor; everything else stands on it.
ONT.ontology: Ontology is a directed acyclic graph of Existence kinds. Root: Existence. Each kind is a RegistryEntry. Extension is by registry, never by primitive expansion.
ONT.taxonomy: By abstraction: Kind / Subkind / Instance-kind. By stability: Foundational / Core / Domain / Ephemeral.
ONT.dataModel:
```yaml
Ontology:
  node: <Identity>
  kind: <registry kind id>
  parentKinds: [<Identity>]
  properties: [<registry property>]
  relationships: [<registry relation kind>]
  source: <Primitive|Projection>
```
ONT.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Proposed
    Proposed --> Approved
    Approved --> Deprecated
```
workflow: propose kind with parent → acyclicity check → approve → publish → existing instances re-project
authorities: Semantic Authority (kind approval); primitive-level changes require Constitutional Assembly.
ONT.privacy: Ontology carries no personal data by design — it is structure, not content.
ONT.audit: Every kind addition/deprecation is logged with rationale and authority; the full history of 'what existed when' is queryable.
ONT.twin: Ontology versions the structure twins are built on; a twin's schema is an ontology projection.
ONT.agent: Ontology Agent proposes new kinds from observed patterns and detects orphaned subkinds.
ONT.runtime: Traversal is cached per node; invalidation on kind approval/deprecation.
ONT.scaling: Small, globally replicated, read-heavy graph. Write path is authority-gated and low-frequency.
ONT.multiTenant: Ontology is shared constitutional truth; tenants extend via projections, never by mutating the core.
ONT.geo: Globally consistent; ontology is not jurisdiction-scoped — applications apply jurisdiction via Context.
ONT.failure: Cycle introduction, orphaned kind, conflicting parents, primitive-level drift.
ONT.recovery: Kinds are versioned; deprecation is reversible while no dependents remain.
ONT.certification: Kind must pass acyclicity, parent existence, property compatibility, and naming uniqueness.
ONT.migration: Ontology evolves only through this domain — schema migration and ontology evolution are the same act.
ONT.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant P as Proposer
    participant ON as Ontology Domain
    P->>ON: propose(kind, parent)
    ON->>ON: acyclicity check
    ON-->>P: OntologyKindApproved
```
ONT.state:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Validating
    Validating --> Acyclic
    Acyclic --> Published
```
ONT.blueprint: Build order for ONT: (1) define registry entries — this domain owns by abstraction: kind / subkind / instance-kind as registry truth, not code; (2) implement the contract surface first (ontology.kind.propose, ontology.kind.approve, ontology.kind.deprecate) and validate against ONT boundaries; (3) event-source all state so history is reconstructable; (4) wire the enforcement points — authority check, policy guard, evidence binding, trace — in-line, with no bypass path; (5) add tests per the Testing Architecture, citing evidence per gate; (6) obtain Verification and Certification before activation. TAX.concepts: Taxonomy is how things are classified. Taxonomy ≠ Ontology (what exists) and ≠ Classification (the act of assigning). Taxonomy is the structure of classification.
TAX.ontology: Taxonomy is a tree/DAG of Categories. Each Category has one canonical parent (tree) or defined parents (DAG), membership rules, and a governing Context.
TAX.taxonomy: By structure: Tree / DAG / Facet. By mutability: Frozen / Governed / Open. By scope: Universal / Domain / Tenant.
TAX.dataModel:
```yaml
Taxonomy:
  categoryRef: <Identity>
  parentCategories: [<Identity>]
  membershipRule: <registry expression>
  governingContext: <Context>
  temporal: {effectiveFrom, effectiveTo}
```
TAX.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Defined
    Defined --> Active
    Active --> Deprecated
```
workflow: create category with rule → assign under governance → reclassify on rule change → preserve history
authorities: Semantic Authority (structure); Context Authority may add domain categories in scope.
TAX.privacy: Classifications of persons are sensitive; category membership over personal data requires consent scope.
TAX.audit: Every assignment and reclassification records who, under which rule, in which context, and when. Prior classifications remain queryable.
TAX.twin: Taxonomy versions structure that classification twins mirror.
TAX.agent: Taxonomy Agent proposes new categories from clustering observations and detects stale classifications.
TAX.runtime: Tree traversal cached; assignment is validated against membership rule at write time.
TAX.scaling: Read-heavy; cache per context. Write path validates full ancestor chain.
TAX.multiTenant: Universal taxonomy is shared; tenant taxonomies are projections layered on top, never mutations of the core.
TAX.geo: Category names are locale-resolved via the Semantic Domain; structure is global.
TAX.failure: Cycle, orphaned category, ambiguous membership, merge conflict.
TAX.recovery: Reclassification is versioned; merges preserve both lineages. No classification is ever lost.
TAX.certification: Category must pass acyclicity, rule validity, context jurisdiction, and naming uniqueness.
TAX.migration: New categories are registry additions; reclassification is governed, never bulk-rewritten.
TAX.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Caller
    participant TA as Taxonomy Domain
    participant CT as Context
    C->>TA: assign(subject, category)
    TA->>TA: validate membership rule
    TA->>CT: confirm governing context
    CT-->>TA: in scope
    TA-->>C: TaxonomyAssigned
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> RuleCheck
    RuleCheck --> ContextCheck
    ContextCheck --> Assigned
```

REA.concepts: The platform supports simultaneous, mutually disagreeing realities that all remain valid within their Context. Physical, Digital, Commercial, Financial, Operational, Legal, Regulatory, Customer, Partner, AI, Predicted, Future, Simulated — each a first-class reality.
REA.ontology: Reality is a Context-scoped projection of primitives. Two realities may contradict and both be valid; resolution is governed, never automatic except by policy.
REA.taxonomy: By actuality: Actual (physical) / Constructed (commercial, legal) / Projected (predicted, simulated) / Consensual (financial). By persistence: Persistent / Ephemeral.
REA.dataModel:
```yaml
Reality:
  realityId: <Identity>
  realityType: <registry id>
  context: <Context>
  subjects: [<Identity>]
  authority: <Authority>
  contradictionPolicy: <Policy>
  temporal: {asOf}
```
REA.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Projected
    Projected --> Contradicted
    Contradicted --> Reconciled
    Contradicted --> Coexisting: policy allows
    Reconciled --> [*]
```
workflow: project primitives into reality type → bind context → detect contradictions → apply contradiction policy → coexist or reconcile
authorities: Reality Authority (reconciliation); each reality's authority governs its own projection.
REA.privacy: Realities containing personal data inherit the strictest applicable consent scope across all contributing contexts.
REA.audit: Every contradiction records both realities, their authorities, and the policy that decided the outcome.
REA.twin: Each reality type can host its own twin fleet — a subject may have distinct twins per reality.
REA.agent: Reality Agent detects cross-reality drift and proposes reconciliation candidates under governance.
REA.runtime: Projection is computed per (subject, realityType, context) and cached; contradiction detection is a stream job.
REA.scaling: Projections are lazily computed and cached by hash; hot subjects are pre-projected.
REA.multiTenant: Tenant realities are isolated; shared realities (e.g., legal) are read-only projections of authoritative domains.
REA.geo: Realities are jurisdiction-scoped; the same subject may have legally distinct realities per region — all valid.
REA.failure: Contradiction deadlock, projection staleness, authority conflict, fork divergence.
REA.recovery: Projections are recomputable from primitives — reality is never backed up, it is re-derived.
REA.certification: Reality must pass context binding, authority validity, and contradiction-policy compliance.
REA.migration: New reality types are registry additions; existing projections re-derive on type change.
REA.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Caller
    participant RE as Reality Domain
    participant CT as Context
    C->>RE: project(subject, realityType)
    RE->>CT: resolve scope
    CT-->>RE: context
    RE->>RE: derive projection
    RE-->>C: RealityProjected
```
REA.state:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Scoping
    Scoping --> Deriving
    Deriving --> ContradictionCheck
    ContradictionCheck --> Published
```
REA.blueprint: Build order for REA: (1) define registry entries — this domain owns by actuality: actual (physical) / constructed (commercial, legal) / projected (predicted, simulated) / consensual (financial) as registry truth, not code; (2) implement the contract surface first (reality.project, reality.contradict, reality.reconcile) and validate against REA boundaries; (3) event-source all state so history is reconstructable; (4) wire the enforcement points — authority check, policy guard, evidence binding, trace — in-line, with no bypass path; (5) add tests per the Testing Architecture, citing evidence per gate; (6) obtain Verification and Certification before activation. Acceptance: the Zero Partial and Law 001 audits pass, every action answers the seven explainability questions, and this domain mutates no other domain internals.

PER.concepts: Perspective is observer-specific interpretation. Perspective ≠ Context: context is the applicability boundary; perspective is who is looking. The same object projects differently to customer, merchant, partner, supplier, regulator, auditor, agent, and AI.
PER.ontology: Perspective has an Observer (Identity or Authority), a subject, and a projection policy. Perspectives never change the subject's truth — only its presentation.
PER.taxonomy: By observer class: Human-role / Organizational / Regulatory / Automated-agent / AI. By fidelity: Full / Filtered / Redacted.
PER.dataModel:
```yaml
Perspective:
  perspectiveId: <Identity>
  observer: <Identity|Authority>
  subject: <Identity>
  projectionPolicy: <Policy>
  redactionPolicy: <Policy>
  context: <Context>
  asOf: <Time>
```
PER.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Registered
    Registered --> Projected
    Projected --> Invalidated
    Invalidated --> [*]
```
workflow: identify observer → resolve policy set → project subject → apply redaction → serve
authorities: Observer's Authority governs what it may see; the subject's Authority governs what may be shown.
PER.privacy: Perspective is the primary privacy control surface: data minimization and redaction are projection-time, not afterthoughts.
PER.audit: Every projection records observer, subject, policies applied, and fields redacted — the basis of disclosure audit.
PER.twin: Perspective drives per-observer twin views — one underlying twin, many safe projections.
PER.agent: Perspective Agent verifies that no projection leaks beyond its policy — an ongoing compliance check.
PER.runtime: Projection is computed per request from policy; results are short-TTL cached keyed by (observer, subject, policy-version).
PER.scaling: Read-heavy; policy evaluation is the hot path and is compiled per policy version.
PER.multiTenant: Cross-tenant perspective is denied absent explicit published relationship and policy.
PER.geo: Observer jurisdiction policy applies at projection time — a regulator's perspective in one region is not valid in another.
PER.failure: Policy conflict between observer grant and subject redaction, stale policy version, projection timeout.
PER.recovery: Projections are recomputable; policy versioning guarantees deterministic re-projection.
PER.certification: Perspective must pass both observer-grant and subject-redaction policy with no unresolved conflict.
PER.migration: New observer classes are registry additions; projections re-derive on policy change.
PER.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant O as Observer
    participant PE as Perspective Domain
    participant PL as Policy
    O->>PE: project(subject)
    PE->>PL: observer grant + subject redaction
    PL-->>PE: effective policy
    PE->>PE: project + redact
    PE-->>O: filtered view
```
PER.state:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Identifying
    Identifying --> PolicyResolving
    PolicyResolving --> Projecting
    Projecting --> Serving
```

UNC.concepts: Uncertainty is first-class. Confidence, probability, ambiguity, competing truths, incomplete knowledge, and unknown knowledge are all modeled explicitly — never hidden behind false precision.
UNC.ontology: Uncertainty attaches to any assertion as a distribution or interval, not a point value. Unknown-ness is a state, not an error: 'we do not know' is a valid, recorded answer.
UNC.taxonomy: By kind: Aleatoric (inherent) / Epistemic (knowledge gap) / Ambiguity (multiple readings) / Conflict (competing truths). By representation: Probability / Interval / Fuzzy / Qualitative.
UNC.dataModel:
```yaml
Uncertainty:
  uncertaintyId: <Identity>
  subject: <Identity>
  kind: <registry id>
  representation: <Probability|Interval|Fuzzy|Qualitative>
  parameters: <registry expression>
  confidence: <0..1>
  alternatives: [<alternative assertions>]
  ambiguity: <registry measure>
  asOf: <Time>
```
UNC.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Attached
    Attached --> Refined: new evidence
    Attached --> Propagated: downstream impact
    Refined --> Escalated: threshold breach
```
workflow: attach uncertainty to assertion → propagate through dependents → refine on evidence → escalate on threshold breach
authorities: Domain Authority (attachment); escalation routed to the owning domain's governance.
UNC.privacy: Uncertainty over personal subjects uses aggregated parameters; individual-level distributions require consent.
UNC.audit: Every refinement records the evidence that moved the estimate — uncertainty provenance is fully traceable.
UNC.twin: Twins expose uncertainty alongside state; a twin that reports certainty without justification is non-compliant.
UNC.agent: Uncertainty Agent monitors thresholds and escalates before downstream decisions over-trust weak assertions.
UNC.runtime: Propagation is a graph traversal recomputing dependent confidences; cached per assertion version.
UNC.scaling: Propagation batches on evidence events; hot assertions are pre-propagated.
UNC.multiTenant: Uncertainty never crosses tenants; shared assertions carry shared uncertainty.
UNC.geo: Estimation standards are jurisdiction-aware; regulatory contexts may require conservative bounds.
UNC.failure: Propagation cycle, over-precise collapse, threshold storm, contradiction with recorded certainty.
UNC.recovery: Estimates recompute from evidence history; attaching uncertainty is reversible by refinement.
UNC.certification: Assertion must declare uncertainty to be used in automated decisions — silent certainty is prohibited.
UNC.migration: New kinds/representations are registry additions; existing estimates re-propagate on kind change.
UNC.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant D as Domain
    participant UN as Uncertainty Domain
    participant KN as Knowledge
    D->>UN: attach(assertion, distribution)
    UN->>UN: propagate to dependents
    UN->>KN: record uncertainty
    KN-->>UN: acknowledged
    UN-->>D: UncertaintyAttached
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Attaching
```

CONTR.concepts: Contradiction is stored, not erased. 'Regulator: Approved' and 'Auditor: Rejected' coexist and both remain valid until governed resolution. Suppressing a contradiction destroys evidence.
CONTR.ontology: Contradiction has two or more Assertions, each with its own Authority and Context, plus a resolution state. Contradiction is a relationship among truths, not an error.
CONTR.taxonomy: By resolution state: Open / Resolved / Unresolvable-by-policy. By severity: Informational / Blocking / Critical. By scope: Local / Cross-jurisdiction / Cross-reality.
CONTR.dataModel:
```yaml
Contradiction:
  contradictionId: <Identity>
  assertions: [{assertion, authority, context}]
  severity: <registry level>
  resolutionState: <Open|Resolved|Unresolvable>
  resolution: <Policy|Decision|null>
  detectedAt: <Time>
  evidence: [<Evidence>]
```
CONTR.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Open
    Open --> Escalated
    Escalated --> Resolved
    Open --> Unresolvable: policy permits coexistence
    Resolved --> [*]
```
workflow: detect across assertions → classify severity → route to resolver authority → resolve or declare coexistence → publish
authorities: Each assertion's authority stands; resolution requires an authority superior to all parties or their consent.
CONTR.privacy: Contradictions involving personal data are access-restricted; the fact of contradiction is auditable, contents are scoped.
CONTR.audit: Both sides of every contradiction are preserved with full evidence, even after resolution. Resolution rationale is mandatory.
CONTR.twin: Contradiction explains twin divergence across realities — the twin system never silently picks one truth.
CONTR.agent: Contradiction Agent continuously scans for new conflicts and stale resolutions, escalating per severity policy.
CONTR.runtime: Detection is a stream over assertion events; open contradictions are cached for resolver dashboards.
CONTR.scaling: Detection batches by subject; resolution is human-or-policy gated, so write throughput is low.
CONTR.multiTenant: Contradictions are tenant-scoped unless they involve shared authoritative assertions.
CONTR.geo: Cross-jurisdiction contradictions may be declared Unresolvable — that is a valid, recorded outcome, not a failure.
CONTR.failure: Detection miss, premature auto-resolution, evidence loss on resolution.
CONTR.recovery: Resolutions are themselves recorded; reopening is first-class and restores the Open state with history.
CONTR.certification: System must prove no contradiction was silently dropped — the audit trail must reconcile with detection events.
CONTR.migration: New severity levels and resolution strategies are registry additions.
CONTR.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant OB as Observer
    participant CO as Contradiction Domain
    participant AU as Authority
    OB->>CO: detect(assertion A, assertion B)
    CO->>CO: classify severity
    CO->>AU: route for resolution
    AU-->>CO: resolution or coexistence
    CO-->>OB: ContradictionResolved
```
CONTR.state:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Detecting
    Detecting --> Classifying
    Classifying --> Routing
    Routing --> Resolved
```
CONTR.blueprint: Build order for CONTR: (1) define registry entries — this domain owns by resolution state: open / resolved / unresolvable-by-policy as registry truth, not code; (2) implement the contract surface first (contradiction.detect, contradiction.resolve, contradiction.escalate) and validate against CONTR boundaries; (3) event-source all state so history is reconstructable; (4) wire the enforcement points — authority check, policy guard, evidence binding, trace — in-line, with no bypass path; (5) add tests per the Testing Architecture, citing evidence per gate; (6) obtain Verification and Certification before activation. Acceptance: the Zero Partial and Law 001 audits pass, every action answers the seven explainability questions, and this domain mutates no other domain internals.

POSS.concepts: Possibility is a realizable future state. Possibility ≠ Simulation (the method) and ≠ Reality (the present). Possibilities are the outputs of simulations and the inputs to planning.
POSS.ontology: Possibility has an origin (Simulation or Reasoning), a subject, a plausibility, and preconditions. Possibilities never claim truth — they claim realizability under conditions.
POSS.taxonomy: By horizon: Immediate / Near / Far. By plausibility: Likely / Possible / Unlikely / Speculative. By desirability: Desired / Neutral / Adverse.
POSS.dataModel:
```yaml
Possibility:
  possibilityId: <Identity>
  subject: <Identity>
  origin: <Simulation|Reasoning>
  preconditions: [<registry expression>]
  plausibility: <0..1>
  desirability: <Desired|Neutral|Adverse>
  temporal: {earliestRealization}
  context: <Context>
```
POSS.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Registered
    Registered --> Evaluated
    Evaluated --> Realized: preconditions met + decision
    Evaluated --> Dismissed
    Realized --> [*]
```
workflow: register from simulation → evaluate plausibility against current state → decide → realize or dismiss with rationale
authorities: Planning Authority (evaluation); realization requires the acting domain's authority.
POSS.privacy: Possibilities about individuals require aggregated or consented inputs; speculative personal futures are prohibited.
POSS.audit: Every possibility records origin, preconditions, and evaluation rationale. Realization links to the Decision that authorized it.
POSS.twin: Possibilities are the forward-looking twin state — what the twin could become, kept strictly separate from what it is.
POSS.agent: Possibility Agent ranks possibilities for planning agents and flags adverse ones for risk review.
POSS.runtime: Evaluation is a precondition check against current state; registered lazily, cached by origin hash.
POSS.scaling: Possibilities are numerous and low-cost; storage is time-bucketed with policy-driven pruning.
POSS.multiTenant: Possibilities never cross tenants; shared possibilities require published relationship.
POSS.geo: Evaluation is jurisdiction-scoped — a possibility legal in one region may be adverse in another.
POSS.failure: Precondition staleness, plausibility inflation, unbounded possibility accumulation.
POSS.recovery: Possibilities are disposable; dismissal is reversible while preconditions still hold.
POSS.certification: Possibility must declare origin, preconditions, and plausibility to inform any plan.
POSS.migration: New horizons and desirability classes are registry additions.
POSS.sequence:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram

    participant PO as Possibility Domain
    participant PL as Planner
    SI->>PO: register(future state)
    PO->>PO: evaluate preconditions
    PL->>PO: request candidates
    PO-->>PL: ranked possibilities
```

POSS.state:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Registering
    Registering --> Evaluating
```

EMG.concepts: Emergence is a property of the whole that is absent from the parts. It is not designed; it is detected. The constitution does not suppress emergence — it governs it.
EMG.ontology: Emergence has a System (a set of relationships), an EmergedProperty, a detection method, and a review state. Emergence is evidence that the system has exceeded the sum of its parts.
EMG.taxonomy: By kind: Behavioral / Structural / Semantic / Economic / Social. By valence: Beneficial / Neutral / Adverse / Hazardous. By stability: Transient / Persistent.
EMG.dataModel:
```yaml
Emergence:
  emergenceId: <Identity>
  system: [<Identity>]
  emergedProperty: <registry id>
  detectionMethod: <registry id>
  evidence: [<Evidence>]
  valence: <Beneficial|Neutral|Adverse|Hazardous>
  stability: <Transient|Persistent>
  reviewState: <Detected|UnderReview|Governing|Governed>
```
EMG.stateMachine:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Detected
    Detected --> UnderReview
    UnderReview --> Governed
    UnderReview --> Escalated
    Escalated --> Governed
```
workflow: detect via observation/agent → classify valence → review → govern (adopt, counter, or monitor) → record
authorities: Governance Authority (adverse/hazardous); any authority may report.
EMG.privacy: Emergent properties over personal populations are aggregated; no individual inference without consent.
EMG.audit: Every emergent property records the system that produced it, the evidence, and the governance decision.
EMG.twin: Emergence is how twin fleets exhibit fleet-level behavior no single twin shows — monitored across the federation.
EMG.agent: Emergence Agent is the primary detector, watching relationship graphs for properties not present in any node.
EMG.runtime: Detection is a batch/stream analytics job; review is governance-gated.
EMG.scaling: Detection scales with relationship volume; results are time-windowed.
EMG.multiTenant: Emergence is detected within a tenant's system; cross-tenant emergence requires federation-level review.
EMG.geo: Emergent behavior crossing jurisdictions triggers review in every affected region.
EMG.failure: Detection lag, false-positive flood, hazardous emergence under-governed.
EMG.recovery: Emergence records are permanent evidence; adverse emergence is countered by policy, not deleted.
EMG.certification: System must demonstrate an emergence review path for any hazardous classification.
EMG.migration: New property kinds and valences are registry additions.
